text:
taylor: Heads-up — I've been seeing steady KV-slot memory growth on Dedicated when sessions hit long contexts (> 50k tokens). Not an immediate OOM but residency keeps creeping up over hours. Logs + heap profiles attached below.

liz: Interesting — same workload on Hosted stays flat? any config drift between deployments? :thinking_face:

taylor: Yep, hosted looks stable. Dedicated and one Private customer repro show similar growth. Suspect eviction isn't reclaiming fragmented slots fast enough when we switch kernels for long sequences.

omar: Can you paste the pprof snippet? also which kernel selection path was triggered? we rolled a kernel tweak last week.

taylor: Paste of top allocation from heap profile (short):
```
heap profile: total 2.1GB
  900MB  kvpage_slots (pinned)
  400MB  pageframe_fragments
  350MB  small-alloc arena
  200MB  transient tensors (garbage)
```
Kernel decision log around the session: `tiny-attn -> fused-kernel-v2 -> fallback-slow` based on estimated seq_len 8k -> 64k ramp.

jess: If fused-kernel-v2 changes memory alignment/stride, that could leave holes when we evict only whole frames. Might explain fragmentation increasing over time.

taylor: Exactly. On Dedicated our allocator uses `page_align = 2MB` but on Hosted it's `page_align = 1MB` (historical tuning). Private onprem customer has hugepage disabled so allocator behavior is different. Config drift likely.

omar: Can we reproduce with a synthetic that toggles kernel at runtime? I can run a microbenchmark that ramps seq length and forces kernel switch points.

liz: Please include metrics we care about: kv_resident_slots, kv_eviction_count, page_frag_bytes, kernel_switch_count. Also add the batching profile (`avg_batch_size`, `batch_wait_ms`) — batching heuristics affect reuse.

taylor: Good list — initial telemetry from repro: 
```
kv_resident_slots: +1.8%/hr
kv_eviction_count: 12/hr
page_frag_bytes: +120MB/hr
kernel_switch_count: 4/session
avg_batch_size: 6 -> peaks 18
batch_wait_ms: 12ms
```

jess: That eviction_count is low given fragmentation growth. Suggest enabling aggressive compaction on Dedicated as a temporary mitigation. We can flip `kv.compact_threshold=0.6` and test.

omar: I'm worried about VPC MTU/driver interactions on Dedicated vs Private. We saw `pageframe_fragments` spike with certain NIC drivers — could be a DMA alignment problem. Any driver/release diffs?

taylor: Dedicated fleets were moved to kernel 6.x + driver 2.3 last month; Hosted remained on 5.x. Private customer's servers are 5.x but with older nvlink firmware. So yes, env differences exist.

liz: Two-pronged plan: (1) repro with kernel-switch microbenchmark + toggles for page_align and compaction; (2) add short-term config flip on one Dedicated pool to `kv.compact_threshold=0.6` and `page_align=1MB` to match Hosted to see if growth flattens.

jess: Also add a batching experiment: force constant small batches vs letting runtime coalesce. If reuse of prefixes is lower because of different batching latency, that could reduce KV reuse and make eviction ineffective.

taylor: I'll run repro + attach pprof and `strace` of allocator calls. Omar — can you also produce a kernel-selection trace for the same sessions? want to correlate switch points to memory jumps.

omar: Yep, will instrument and create a flamegraph of kernel selection vs memory allocations.

infra-bot: @taylor created a perf job: perf/dedicated-kv-longctx-2024-11-14 (queued)

liz: If the quick config flip helps, we should roll a canary to one Dedicated shard and monitor cost delta — compaction is CPU-y and may increase latency. Add rollback criteria: >5% p99 latency increase or >10% CPU spike.

jess: Good call. Also add an alert for sudden kernel_switch_count spikes — that's a clear signal for this class of regressions.

taylor: Action items:
- taylor: run microbenchmark + pprof + strace (ETA 3h)
- omar: instrument kernel selection traces and flamegraphs (ETA 5h)
- liz: prepare canary config (kv.compact_threshold, page_align) + monitor dashboard + rollback rules (ETA 2h)
- jess: batching experiment and add alert rules (ETA 6h)

taylor: One more note — customer on Private reported disk-backed KV paging enabling when GPU memory pressure hits 95%. Need to confirm if our fallback to disk has different eviction semantics (sync vs async) — that matters for reuse.

omar: I'll inspect disk-paging path, might be blocking IO and leading to delayed frees.

liz: Thanks — keep updates here. If anyone finds a quick patch to force compaction at safe points (e.g., after kernel switch) that might be the least risky fix.

jess: :thumbsup:

taylor: Will post results and artifacts in this thread. Thanks all.
